title: Grade 12 Physics — Electric Charges & Fields and Electrostatic Potential
description: Electric Charges and Fields and Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance practice questions
subject: physics

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is:
options: Proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to the distance
Proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance
Proportional to the square of the distance
questions.explanation: F = kq₁q₂/r². The force is proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance. This is Coulomb's law.

questions.question: The SI unit of electric field intensity is:
questions.explanation: Electric field E = F/q. Units = Newton/Coulomb = N/C. Since 1 V = 1 J/C and 1 J = 1 N·m, N/C = V/m.

questions.question: The total charge enclosed by a closed surface is related to the electric flux through Gauss's law as:
questions.explanation: Gauss's law: Φ = q_enc/ε₀. The total electric flux through any closed surface equals the net charge enclosed divided by the permittivity of free space ε₀.

questions.question: Electric field lines always:
options: Start on positive charges and end on negative charges
Are always perpendicular to each other
questions.explanation: Electric field lines start on (originate from) positive charges and end on (terminate at) negative charges. They never cross, and their density indicates field strength.

questions.question: The electric field inside a uniformly charged hollow metallic sphere is:
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, inside a hollow conductor, the enclosed charge is zero. Therefore, E = 0 inside a closed metallic shell.

questions.question: Quantisation of charge means that:
options: Charge can take any continuous value
Charge is always a multiple of the elementary charge e (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
Charge is the same as mass
questions.explanation: Charge is quantised: q = ne, where n is an integer and e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C is the elementary charge. Fractional charges of quarks exist inside protons but are not observed freely.

questions.question: Electric potential V at a point is defined as:
options: Work done per unit charge to move a test charge from infinity to that point
questions.explanation: Electric potential V = W/q₀. It is the work done (by an external agent) per unit positive test charge in bringing it from infinity to the given point, without acceleration.

questions.question: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with plate area A, separation d, and dielectric constant K is:
questions.explanation: C = Kε₀A/d. Without dielectric (K=1): C = ε₀A/d. The dielectric increases capacitance by factor K.

questions.question: Equipotential surfaces are always:
questions.explanation: Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to electric field lines. No work is done in moving a charge along an equipotential surface since ΔV = 0.

questions.question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to voltage V is:
questions.explanation: Energy stored U = ½CV². This can also be written as Q²/(2C) = QV/2.

questions.question: When capacitors are connected in series, the equivalent capacitance is:
questions.explanation: For two capacitors in series: 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ → C = C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂). Series reduces capacitance; parallel increases it.

questions.question: The SI unit of electric potential is:
questions.explanation: Electric potential is measured in Volts (V). 1 Volt = 1 Joule/Coulomb (J/C). The Farad is the unit of capacitance.

questions.question: The relation between electric field E and potential V is:
options: E = V/d only in parallel plates
questions.explanation: E = −dV/dx (negative gradient of potential). The minus sign means E points from high potential to low potential (in the direction of decreasing V).

questions.question: Dielectric strength refers to:
options: Maximum electric field a dielectric can withstand without breaking down
questions.explanation: Dielectric strength is the maximum electric field (in V/m) that an insulating material can withstand without electrical breakdown (sparking through it).

questions.question: Two capacitors of 4 μF and 6 μF are connected in parallel. The equivalent capacitance is:
questions.explanation: Capacitors in parallel: C = C₁ + C₂ = 4 + 6 = 10 μF. Parallel connection always increases capacitance.
